$comment: Single source of truth for the Data Table API. Every framework package is tested against this file.
name: data-table
title: Data Table
description: A table you can sort, filter, select rows in and page through.

columns.type: { key; header; cell?; sortValue?; filterValue?; sortable?; numeric? }[]
columns.description: What each column shows. Columns sort unless sortable is false; numeric right-aligns them.

data.description: The rows. Sorting, filtering and paging happen in the browser.

label.description: Names the table's scrolling region (and the filter box).

pageSize.description: Rows per page; 0 shows them all. The pager is Pagination's simple version.

selectable.description: A checkbox per row and a "select all" checkbox in the header, which shows a dash when some rows are selected.

defaultSelected / onSelectionChange.description: Rows selected at first, and a callback with the keys after each change.

filterable.description: A search box that hides rows whose text doesn't match.

filterLabel / filterPlaceholder.description: The filter box's name (default "Filter invoices") and placeholder.

defaultSort.description: Sort on first render. Clicking a header sorts ascending, then descending.

rowLabel.description: Name of a row's checkbox. Default: "Select" + the first column.

sort value (HTML).description: In HTML, cells sort by their text (numbers like ₹12,400 sort as numbers). Put data-value on a cell to sort by something else.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Sort by a header, filter by text, select rows and page through 12 invoices, five at a time. In HTML, add data-vin-data-table (and data-page-size) and include vinui.js; every row is in the markup and the script hides the ones on other pages.

examples.title: Sorting only
examples.description: Starts sorted by commits, highest first. Click a header to sort by it; click again to reverse.

examples.title: Selection
examples.description: Two rows start selected, so the header checkbox shows a dash (mixed). Clicking it selects every row.

a11y: A real table with th[scope] headers. Sortable headers hold a button, and the sorted column has aria-sort="ascending" or "descending", so screen readers say how it's sorted.
The sort arrows are hidden from screen readers; the button's name is the column name.
Each row checkbox has a name ("Select INV-1042"). The header checkbox is "Select all rows" and is mixed (indeterminate) when some are selected.
The status line ("2 of 12 selected") is a polite live region, so changes are announced.
The filter box is a labelled search input; paging uses Pagination's Previous / Next buttons, which are disabled at the ends.
On small screens the table scrolls sideways inside its focusable region instead of squashing the columns.
